sentences.zh: 今天的节目由 T-Mobile for Business 赞助播出。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I recently visited Mexico City and paid a visit to the National Museum of Anthropology.
sentences.zh: 我最近去了墨西哥城，参观了国立人类学博物馆。

sentences.en: In a series of chambers, the museum depicts the rise and fall of various cultures in Mexico's history.
sentences.zh: 博物馆通过一系列展厅，展现了墨西哥历史上各种文化的兴衰。

sentences.en: One thing that struck me was the staggering range of religious beliefs
sentences.zh: 令我震惊的是，宗教信仰的范围竟然如此之广，

sentences.en: that rose to prominence and then faded away over the centuries.
sentences.zh: 它们在几个世纪里崛起、崭露头角，随后又消逝。

sentences.en: The Temple of the Feathered Serpent, for example, was a major religious center at Teotihuacan.
sentences.zh: 例如，羽蛇神庙是特奥蒂瓦坎的主要宗教中心。

sentences.en: Built around 2,000 years ago, the magnificent pyramid likely paid homage to a storm god.
sentences.zh: 这座宏伟的金字塔大约建于两千年前，很可能是为了向风暴之神致敬。

sentences.en: When archaeologists explored the structure, they found it concealed horrors.
sentences.zh: 当考古学家探索这座建筑时，他们发现其中隐藏着恐怖的东西。

sentences.en: Among them, a series of skeletons bounded the wrists and laid symmetrically side by side,
sentences.zh: 其中包括一系列手腕被捆绑、对称并排摆放的骨架，

sentences.en: victims possibly sacrificed to soothe an angry deity.
sentences.zh: 这些受害者可能是为了安抚愤怒的神明而被献祭的。

sentences.en: Some time later, I came by an account of another storm god.
sentences.zh: 一段时间后，我偶然读到了一份关于另一个风暴之神的记载。

sentences.en: This god, who worshipped centuries earlier in ancient Greece, had a dramatic origin story.
sentences.zh: 这位神明在几个世纪前的古希腊受到崇拜，有着戏剧性的身世背景。

sentences.en: The titan Kronos, the son of Uranus and Mother Earth, is believed to have castrated and deposed his father.
sentences.zh: 据信，泰坦克洛诺斯是天王乌拉诺斯和大地母亲的儿子，他阉割并废黜了自己的父亲。

sentences.en: Fearful that his children would do the same to him, he ate them.
sentences.zh: 由于害怕自己的孩子也会这样对待他，他把他们都吃掉了。

sentences.en: All except Zeus, who went on to overthrow him and become one of the most important gods of ancient Greece.
sentences.zh: 除了宙斯，宙斯后来推翻了他，成为了古希腊最重要的神灵之一。

sentences.en: Zeus had many powers, among them the ability to control the weather.
sentences.zh: 宙斯拥有许多法力，其中包括控制天气的气象能力。

sentences.en: Around the world, we see a staggering range of religious faiths,
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，我们都能看到种类繁多的宗教信仰，

sentences.en: as well as similarities in beliefs in very different times and places.
sentences.zh: 以及在截然不同的时代和地点中信仰的相似之处。

sentences.en: Given the ubiquity of these beliefs, psychologists have long speculated about how these beliefs shape
sentences.zh: 鉴于这些信仰的无处不在，心理学家长期以来一直在推测这些信仰是如何塑造

sentences.en: and are shaped by the human mind.
sentences.zh: 以及被人类心灵所塑造的。

sentences.en: Today, we explore features in the brain that are intimately tied to our capacity for religious belief.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来探讨那些与我们宗教信仰能力紧密相连的大脑特征。

sentences.en: We also look at how all of us, religious and non-religious people alike,
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨我们所有人——无论是信教者还是不信教者——

sentences.en: can use this knowledge to find more meaning in our lives.
sentences.zh: 如何利用这些知识在生活中寻找更多意义。

sentences.en: God and the mind, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 神灵与大脑，本周《隐藏的大脑》为您播出。

sentences.en: For centuries, the country of Lebanon prided itself on being a richly multicultural place.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，黎巴嫩这个国家一直以其丰富的多元文化而自豪。

sentences.en: It was home to a multitude of ethnic and religious groups, Christians and Muslims, Arabs and Armenians, Druze and Jews, all living together.
sentences.zh: 这里是众多族群和宗教团体的家园：基督徒与穆斯林、阿拉伯人与亚美尼亚人、德鲁兹人与犹太人，大家共同生活在一起。

sentences.en: After it was occupied by the French, tourists affectionately nicknamed its capital Beirut the Paris of the Middle East for its cafes, thriving universities, and robust art scene.
sentences.zh: 在被法国占领后，游客们亲切地给它的首都贝鲁特起了个绰号，叫“中东的巴黎”，因为这里有咖啡馆、蓬勃发展的大学和充满活力的艺术氛围。

sentences.en: Ara Norenzayan grew up in this multi-religious melting pot in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 阿拉·诺伦扎扬在 20 世纪 70 年代的这个多元宗教大熔炉中长大。

sentences.en: Yeah, so my heritage is Armenian.
sentences.zh: 对，所以我的血统是亚美尼亚人。

sentences.en: So the Armenian community is a small and distinctive community in Lebanon.
sentences.zh: 亚美尼亚社群是黎巴嫩一个规模较小且特点鲜明的社群。

sentences.en: Armenians have always been very connected to their history.
sentences.zh: 亚美尼亚人一直与他们的历史紧密相连。

sentences.en: And in particular, the Armenian Apostolic Church, which dates back to the 4th century.
sentences.zh: 尤其是可以追溯到公元 4 世纪的亚美尼亚使徒教会。

sentences.en: So it's one of the oldest living churches on the planet.
sentences.zh: 所以它是地球上现存最古老的教会之一。

sentences.en: So 1,700 years of history.
sentences.zh: 也就是 1700 年的历史。

sentences.en: That was also part of how I grew up, and I was also engaging with that and trying to make sense of it as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是我成长经历的一部分，我也一直在接触它，并试着去理解它。

sentences.en: As a young child, Ara served as an altar boy in his church.
sentences.zh: 小的时候，阿拉曾在他的教堂里担任辅祭男孩。

sentences.en: He mostly attended Mass because his father made him, following the ancient global tradition of children reluctantly obeying their parents.
sentences.zh: 他去参加弥撒主要是因为他父亲逼他去的，这延续了全球孩子们不情愿地顺从父母的古老传统。

sentences.en: He felt like a fly on the wall,
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己就像墙上的苍蝇，

sentences.en: observing the choreographed rituals
sentences.zh: 观察着那些

sentences.en: that his community had performed for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 他的社群已经表演了数百年的编排好的仪式。

sentences.en: He watched his fellow parishioners as they burned incense,
sentences.zh: 他看着身边的教友焚烧香料，

sentences.en: said the Lord's Prayer, and took Holy Communion.
sentences.zh: 诵读主祷文，并领受圣餐。

sentences.en: Easter each year was a time of high drama in Beirut.
sentences.zh: 对贝鲁特来说，每年的复活节都是一出大戏。

sentences.en: I do remember seeing some processions
sentences.zh: 我还记得确实看到了一些游行，

sentences.en: in the neighborhoods where I grew up,
sentences.zh: 在我长大的街区里，

sentences.en: where during Easter, for example,
sentences.zh: 比如在复活节期间，

sentences.en: there would be like dramatic theatrical displays of religiosity for example in in some of the
sentences.zh: 会有那种充满戏剧性的宗教表演，比如在某些

sentences.en: catholic areas you would see that would reenact the crucifixion of jesus and people really felt
sentences.zh: 天主教地区，你会看到他们重演耶稣受难的场景，人们真的感到

sentences.en: enraptured by these experiences someone who would play the role of christ and would carry the cross
sentences.zh: 被这些经历深深吸引，有人扮演基督并背着十字架

sentences.en: And there would be people who were, you know, reenacting the, you know, the Roman soldiers, the whole story of how Jesus was crucified.
sentences.zh: 还有人扮演罗马士兵，重现耶稣如何被钉在十字架上的整个故事。

sentences.en: In many communities this is done, even today, and it can be very emotional and very powerful.
sentences.zh: 在许多社区，直到今天人们依然这样做，这可能非常具有情感冲击力和感染力。

sentences.en: Ara witnessed firsthand how faith ordered the world around him.
sentences.zh: 阿拉亲眼见证了信仰是如何规范他周围的世界的。

sentences.en: Growing up in Lebanon, friends mostly belonged to the same religious communities.
sentences.zh: 在黎巴嫩长大时，朋友们大多属于相同的宗教社群。

sentences.en: Holidays centered on religious festivals.
sentences.zh: 节日以宗教庆典为中心。

sentences.en: ID cards listed people's religions.
sentences.zh: 身份证上会列出人们的宗教信仰。

sentences.en: In 1975, a civil war broke out
sentences.zh: 1975 年，内战爆发了，

sentences.en: and the multicultural bonds that kept the Lebanese people together came apart.
sentences.zh: 将黎巴嫩人民凝聚在一起的多元文化纽带破裂了。

sentences.en: The conflict initially pitted Christians against Muslims,
sentences.zh: 这场冲突最初是基督徒与穆斯林的对抗，

sentences.en: but it quickly escalated and swallowed every group in the country.
sentences.zh: 但它迅速升级，吞噬了国家里的每一个群体。

sentences.en: The Beirut that Ara knew splintered in half.
sentences.zh: 阿拉所熟悉的贝鲁特分裂成了两半。

sentences.en: We had difficulty crossing the green line, it was called.
sentences.zh: 我们很难穿过被称为“绿线”的交界处。

sentences.en: Beirut was divided into East Beirut and West Beirut.
sentences.zh: 贝鲁特被分为东贝鲁特和西贝鲁特。

sentences.en: I lived in East Beirut, which was predominantly Christian.
sentences.zh: 我住在东贝鲁特，那里主要居住着基督徒。

sentences.en: West Beirut was predominantly Muslim, but not entirely.
sentences.zh: 西贝鲁特主要居住着穆斯林，但并非全部如此。

sentences.en: It was still a very diverse place in both sides.
sentences.zh: 双方其实都依然是一个非常多元化的地方。

sentences.en: Our school was in West Beirut.
sentences.zh: 我们的学校在西贝鲁特。

sentences.en: My elementary school that I went to initially was in West Beirut.
sentences.zh: 我最初上的小学在西贝鲁特。

sentences.en: And we lived in East Beirut.
sentences.zh: 而我们住在东贝鲁特。

sentences.en: I mean, the distances are not great.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，距离并不远。

sentences.en: We're talking about like maybe 5, 10 kilometers at moSt.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的最多也就是 5、10 公里左右。

sentences.en: But the division was quite stark,
sentences.zh: 但这种分裂相当鲜明，

sentences.en: and I do remember that crossing that line became dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我记得过这条线变得很危险。

sentences.en: There were snipers, there were bombs.
sentences.zh: 有狙击手，有炸弹。

sentences.en: Sporadically, schools would close.
sentences.zh: 学校偶尔会停课。

sentences.en: I remember my dad in the mornings would listen to the radio
sentences.zh: 我记得我爸爸早晨会听收音机，

sentences.en: to find out if it was safe for us to go to school.
sentences.zh: 来弄清楚我们去上学是否安全。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It was terrifying,
sentences.zh: 这太吓人了，

sentences.en: And I do remember that they were very worried, but they also wanted us to go to school.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得他们非常担心，但他们也希望我们去上学。

sentences.en: And we still had a life in the city, and sometimes we had to go and see friends or meet people.
sentences.zh: 我们在城里仍然有生活，有时我们不得不去见朋友或与人见面。

sentences.en: So it was a tough calculation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个艰难的权衡。

sentences.en: People could find sometimes, figure out places where it was safer to cross than others.
sentences.zh: 人们有时能找到、弄清楚哪些地方过马路比其他地方更安全。

sentences.en: But it also depended on the time and, you know, the rumors about where the snipers are.
sentences.zh: 但这也要看时间，还有关于狙击手在哪里的传言。

sentences.en: So it was really, it does sound really remarkably dangerous, but it was part of our lives and we had to adapt to the circumstances.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来确实非常危险，但这是我们生活的一部分，我们必须适应这种环境。

sentences.en: We couldn't just hold up in our home and stay, not go outside.
sentences.zh: 我们不能只是躲在家里呆着，不出门。

sentences.en: We had to live.
sentences.zh: 我们必须生活。

sentences.en: Did you see any of this firsthand?
sentences.zh: 你亲眼看到过这些吗？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously it was all around you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然这一切都在你身边。

sentences.en: The news was all around you.
sentences.zh: 新闻就在你的周围。

sentences.en: But how close did you actually get to the violence?
sentences.zh: 但你实际上离暴力有多近？

sentences.en: Did it reach your block, your home?
sentences.zh: 它蔓延到你的街区、你的家了吗？

sentences.en: It varied, and there were sporadic fighting when the Civil War broke out.
sentences.zh: 情况各不相同，内战爆发时会有零星的战斗。

sentences.en: But eventually we were, and in two different ways.
sentences.zh: 但最终我们经历了，而且是以两种不同的方式。

sentences.en: One was when there was fighting going on between the different militias,
sentences.zh: 一种是不同民兵组织之间发生战斗时，

sentences.en: and we would have to go in an underground shelter.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不去地下避难所。

sentences.en: It was actually an underground parking lot, and we would just stay there until the fighting would stop.
sentences.zh: 那实际上是一个地下停车场，我们就呆在那里直到战斗停止。

sentences.en: The second one was more terrorism.
sentences.zh: 第二种则是更偏向恐怖主义的形式。

sentences.en: One time, I do remember, we were in a living room of our apartment where we lived,
sentences.zh: 有一次，我确实记得，我们当时在我们住的公寓的起居室里，

sentences.en: and all of a sudden a bomb exploded just outside of the building.
sentences.zh: 突然一颗炸弹在大楼外爆炸了。

sentences.en: And the shards of the bomb spread all over the building, and it hit our kitchen.
sentences.zh: 炸弹的碎片散落在大楼各处，击中了我们的厨房。

sentences.en: And luckily, no one was in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，厨房里没有人。

sentences.en: If there was someone in the kitchen, it would have been injured or died.
sentences.zh: 如果当时厨房里有人，就会受伤或死亡。

sentences.en: Ara realized he was seeing another side of religion.
sentences.zh: 阿拉意识到他看到了宗教的另一面。

sentences.en: The beliefs that his family, his friends, and community shared
sentences.zh: 他的家人、朋友和社区共同拥有的信仰，

sentences.en: now mark friend from foe.
sentences.zh: 现在成了区分敌友的标志。

sentences.en: Fate spilled over into fanaticism and fear.
sentences.zh: 命运演变成了狂热与恐惧。

sentences.en: There was a friend of mine who I played soccer with,
sentences.zh: 我有一个一起踢足球的朋友，

sentences.en: and his school bus was going to drop him off after school
sentences.zh: 他的校车放学后正要送他回家，

sentences.en: and passed by an area where there was a car bomb that exploded
sentences.zh: 经过一个发生汽车炸弹爆炸的区域，

sentences.en: and the whole bus burned down.
sentences.zh: 整辆车都烧毁了。

sentences.en: It was really gut-wrenching and tragic.
sentences.zh: 这真的让人痛心疾首、悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: and I was just told that, you know, your friend died.
sentences.zh: 然后我被告知，你知道的，你的朋友死了。

sentences.en: So it was really a very difficult time.
sentences.zh: 所以那真的是一段非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: I'm curious how your parents explained what was going on to you.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你的父母是如何向你解释当时发生的事情的。

sentences.en: Did you have questions for them?
sentences.zh: 你问过他们问题吗？

sentences.en: Did they try and explain what was going on to you?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有试图向你解释到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: They tried, although they didn't know themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们试过了，尽管他们自己也不知道。

sentences.en: You know, it was so chaotic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时太混乱了。

sentences.en: You know, the trigger for the war was that there was this Christian militia
sentences.zh: 你知道，引发战争的导火索是一个基督教民兵组织

sentences.en: that attacked a Palestinian bus that then spiraled into a fight
sentences.zh: 袭击了一辆巴勒斯坦人的公共汽车，随后演变成了一场

sentences.en: between Christian militias and Palestinian militias.
sentences.zh: 基督教民兵与巴勒斯坦民兵之间的战斗。

sentences.en: But then the war widened into more like a Christian versus Muslim war.
sentences.zh: 但后来战争扩大了，更像是一场基督徒对穆斯林的战争。

sentences.en: But then it degenerated into even more chaos
sentences.zh: 但随后它堕落成了更大的混乱，

sentences.en: where militias within these religious communities
sentences.zh: 这些宗教社群内部的民兵

sentences.en: were fighting against each other and allying with each other.
sentences.zh: 互相战斗，又互相结盟。

sentences.en: So at some point, it made no sense anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，这一切彻底说不通了。

sentences.en: It was just chaos.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是混乱。

sentences.en: And so it was really hard.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很艰难。

sentences.en: They really struggled to explain what was going on.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很艰难地试图解释发生了什么。

sentences.en: And one thing that I remember, it was really struck me as a young person growing up there was how fragile society was around me.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一件事让我作为在那里长大的年轻人深有感触，那就是我周围的社会是多么脆弱。

sentences.en: I could see how easily the social institutions that we rely on could just break down, you know, without enough trust,
sentences.zh: 我能看到我们赖以生存的社会机构是多么轻易地就会崩溃，如果在没有足够信任的情况下，

sentences.en: without enough social solidarity and connections across different ethnic and religious lines.
sentences.zh: 在缺乏跨越不同族裔和宗教界限的社会凝聚力和联系的情况下。

sentences.en: everybody withdrew into their tribal communities,
sentences.zh: 每个人都退回到各自的部族社群中，

sentences.en: and from there it just spiraled out of control.
sentences.zh: 从那以后局势就彻底失控了。

sentences.en: I'm wondering what you started to notice about religious beliefs.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你开始注意到宗教信仰的哪些变化。

sentences.en: One of the things you mentioned to me a moment ago
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到的一点是，

sentences.en: was that people essentially retreated into their religious enclaves
sentences.zh: 随着冲突开始升级，人们基本上退守到了各自的宗教领地中，

sentences.en: as the conflict started to spiral,
sentences.zh: 随着冲突开始升级，

sentences.en: that they found in some ways either comfort or security
sentences.zh: 他们通过与和自己相似的人在一起，在某种程度上找到了慰藉或安全感。

sentences.en: in being among others who are like themselves.
sentences.zh: 随着战争的拖延，

sentences.en: Did you notice other things about people's religious attitudes and beliefs
sentences.zh: 你是否还注意到人们在宗教态度和信仰上的其他事情？

sentences.en: as the war dragged on?
sentences.zh: 随着战争的拖延，

sentences.en: I did notice that people were very passionate about their religious identities and so that was something that it was always on my mind to watch how these religious communities that otherwise are quite similar in the large scheme of things had very strong identities that divided them.
sentences.zh: 我确实注意到人们对他们的宗教身份充满热情，所以我一直在观察这些在宏观层面上其实相当相似的宗教社群，如何拥有将他们分裂的强烈身份认同。

sentences.en: I also saw that people would take refuge in their religious beliefs and practices as a way of shielding themselves from the suffering that was happening around them.
sentences.zh: 我还看到人们会把宗教信仰和习俗当作避难所，以此来保护自己免受周围苦难的折磨。

sentences.en: I do remember that even though arguably the civil war was not a religious war, people were not fighting because of theological disputes or anything like that,
sentences.zh: 我确实记得，尽管可以说内战并不是一场宗教战争，人们打仗也不是因为神学争端之类的原因，

sentences.en: but religion became implicated very quickly.
sentences.zh: 但宗教很快就被牵扯进去了。

sentences.en: So you could see a lot of religious symbolism.
sentences.zh: 所以你能看到很多宗教象征符号。

sentences.en: You know, militia members would have their crosses on the Christian side
sentences.zh: 你知道，民兵成员在基督教这一侧会佩戴十字架

sentences.en: and their Muslim symbolism in the other side.
sentences.zh: 而另一面则是他们的穆斯林象征。

sentences.en: And so that made me also think about why is this so important enough
sentences.zh: 这也让我开始思考，为什么这会如此重要，

sentences.en: that people are using it as a way of identifying with it
sentences.zh: 以至于人们用它来作为一种认同方式，

sentences.en: in opposition to someone who is different from them.
sentences.zh: 来对抗那些与他们不同的人。

sentences.en: As you can see, young Ara had the makings of a social scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 正如你所看到的，年轻的阿拉很有社会科学家的潜质。

sentences.en: Even amid the chaos of the Civil War, he was busy observing things,
sentences.zh: 甚至在内战的混乱中，他也一直在忙着观察事物，

sentences.en: wondering why people believed what they believed.
sentences.zh: 琢磨人们为什么会相信他们所相信的东西。

sentences.en: In time, after his family moved to the United States,
sentences.zh: 后来，他的家人搬到了美国，

sentences.en: Ara became a psychologist who studied the very questions he had wrestled with as a small boy.
sentences.zh: 阿拉成为了一名心理学家，专门研究他小时候曾苦苦思索的那些问题。

sentences.en: How did people come to their religious beliefs?
sentences.zh: 人们是如何产生宗教信仰的？

sentences.en: Why did they believe what they believed?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会相信自己所相信的？

sentences.en: What are the features of the human mind that make possible our immense capacity for faith?
sentences.zh: 人类头脑中究竟有哪些特征，才让我们拥有如此巨大的信仰能力？

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Ara Norenzayan is a psychologist at the University of British Columbia.
sentences.zh: 阿拉·诺伦扎扬是英属哥伦比亚大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: He has long sought to understand how the human mind appears to be designed for religious faith.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，他一直试图理解人类的大脑似乎是如何为宗教信仰而设计的。

sentences.en: Over the course of many years, Ara and other researchers have explored the evolution of religion
sentences.zh: 多年来，阿拉和其他研究人员一直在探索宗教的演变，

sentences.en: and why different religions have risen and fallen during the long march of human history.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么在人类历史的长河中，不同的宗教会兴起又衰落。

sentences.en: We explored some of these ideas in an earlier episode of Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 我们在《隐藏的大脑》之前的一期节目中探讨过其中一些观点。

sentences.en: It was called Creating God, and it featured one of ARA's collaborators, Azim Sharif.
sentences.zh: 那期节目叫做《创造上帝》，其中采访了阿拉的合作者之一阿齐姆·谢里夫。

sentences.en: In a different line of research, ARA has also thought deeply
sentences.zh: 在另一条研究路线中，阿拉也深入思考过

sentences.en: about the features in the human mind that make religious belief possible.
sentences.zh: 人类大脑中使宗教信仰成为可能的那些特征。

sentences.en: Our mental architecture plays a really big role
sentences.zh: 我们的心理结构在很大程度上

sentences.en: in the way that we entertain religious beliefs and practices
sentences.zh: 决定了我们如何以可预测的方式

sentences.en: around the world in predictable ways.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地抱持宗教信仰和进行宗教实践。

sentences.en: One of these, he says,
sentences.zh: 他说，其中之一

sentences.en: is our ability to see human-like qualities
sentences.zh: 就是我们在非人类实体身上

sentences.en: in non-human entities.
sentences.zh: 看到人类般特质的能力。

sentences.en: So there's this tendency to project human features
sentences.zh: 因此，人们有一种将人类特征投射到

sentences.en: to the natural world.
sentences.zh: 自然世界的倾向。

sentences.en: This capacity to anthropomorphize
sentences.zh: 这种将非人拟人化的能力

sentences.en: is a very big part of the way our brains function.
sentences.zh: 是我们大脑运作方式中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And historically, it goes back to ancestral humans
sentences.zh: 从历史来看，这可以追溯到远古人类

sentences.en: trying to make sense of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 试图理解自然世界的努力。

sentences.en: When they saw faces in the clouds or heard voices in the winds,
sentences.zh: 当他们在云中看到人脸或在风中听到声音时，

sentences.en: they were anthropomorphizing.
sentences.zh: 他们就是在进行拟人化。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons why this is such an important part of the human brain
sentences.zh: 这也是人类大脑如此重要的一部分，原因之一在于

sentences.en: is that it helps us also not only understand but also predict how things work
sentences.zh: 它不仅能帮助我们理解，还能帮助我们预测事物的运作方式，

sentences.en: because one of the more important parts of how we understand the world
sentences.zh: 因为我们理解世界的一个更重要的部分

sentences.en: is our social interactions with our humans.
sentences.zh: 就是我们与同类之间的社会交往。

sentences.en: From our earliest days on the planet,
sentences.zh: 从我们来到这个星球的最早日子起，

sentences.en: humans relied on one another for help, for protection, for community.
sentences.zh: 人类就相互依赖以获得帮助、保护和社区。

sentences.en: Humans who were
sentences.zh: 那些

sentences.en: skilled at social interaction, at reading the intentions and minds of fellow humans,
sentences.zh: 擅长社会交往、善于解读同类意图和思想的人类

sentences.en: had an edge.
sentences.zh: 占据了优势。

sentences.en: They became more likely to survive and pass on their genes and their skills to their
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能生存下来，并将他们的基因和技能传递给他们的

sentences.en: descendants.
sentences.zh: 后代。

sentences.en: Once natural selection rewarded the capacity to infer the aims of other humans,
sentences.zh: 一旦自然选择奖励了推断他人目的的能力，

sentences.en: This skill began to be used in other ways.
sentences.zh: 这种技能就开始被用于其他方面。

sentences.en: Humans started to see signs of intention and agency,
sentences.zh: 人类开始在不仅仅是彼此身上，而是在所有地方

sentences.en: not just in each other, but everywhere.
sentences.zh: 都看到意图和能动性的迹象。

sentences.en: You imbue the world, the natural world, with these kinds of spirits.
sentences.zh: 你为世界，即自然世界，注入了这些类型的精神。

sentences.en: Mountains have spirits and rivers can have these agentic qualities.
sentences.zh: 山脉有精灵，河流也可以具有这种能动性的特质。

sentences.en: Natural events like hurricanes or earthquakes
sentences.zh: 飓风或地震等自然现象

sentences.en: evoke also these kinds of agentic understanding of the world.
sentences.zh: 也会唤起对世界的这种能动性理解。

sentences.en: And then from there, it's a small step to then understand or conceptualize gods or spirits as being separate, but controlling these events.
sentences.zh: 从那里出发，只需一小步，就可以将神灵或精灵理解或概念化为独立但控制这些事件的存在。

sentences.en: So that's probably the next stage of our religious evolution.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是我们宗教演化的下一个阶段。

sentences.en: There is tremendous diversity in the way that people understand their gods and spirits and other supernatural beings.
sentences.zh: 人们对神灵、精灵和其他超自然存在的理解存在着巨大的多样性。

sentences.en: But one thing that seems to be quite common around the world and throughout history is that these gods and spirits have human-like qualities.
sentences.zh: 但世界各地和整个历史上似乎有一个非常普遍的共同点，那就是这些神灵和精灵都具有类人的特质。

sentences.en: In some cultures and traditions, it could even be physical human-like qualities.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化和传统中，这甚至可能是物理上的类人特质。

sentences.en: They could have bodies and, for example, many Hindu gods have that.
sentences.zh: 他们可以有身体，例如，许多印度教神明就是如此。

sentences.en: But also, even if they don't have physical qualities, they surely have mental qualities that are human-like.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使他们没有身体特质，他们也肯定拥有类人的精神特质。

sentences.en: And that is even more common around the world.
sentences.zh: 这在世界各地甚至更为普遍。

sentences.en: which, again, verifies this idea that our intramomorphic tendencies
sentences.zh: 这再次验证了这样一个观点：我们的拟人化倾向

sentences.en: feature prominently in the way that our religious mind operates.
sentences.zh: 在我们的宗教头脑运作方式中占据了突出的地位。

sentences.en: In the Judeo-Christian Bible, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，在犹太教和基督教的圣经中，

sentences.en: God is empathetic but also hot-tempered,
sentences.zh: 上帝既善解人意又暴躁，

sentences.en: merciful but judgmental, loving and also jealous.
sentences.zh: 既仁慈又爱审判人，既充满爱心又嫉贤妒能。

sentences.en: In other words, very human-like.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，非常像人类。

sentences.en: The Bible actually explicitly addresses this question
sentences.zh: 圣经其实明确地探讨了这个问题，

sentences.en: by saying that God created humans in his own image.
sentences.zh: 它说上帝是按照自己的形象创造了人类。

sentences.en: One way that Ara and other scholars have explored
sentences.zh: 阿拉和其他学者探索宗教信仰

sentences.en: the cognitive architecture of religious belief
sentences.zh: 认知结构的方法之一，

sentences.en: is by studying the contrast between theological doctrines,
sentences.zh: 就是通过研究神学教义

sentences.en: the way holy books talk about religion,
sentences.zh: （即圣典谈论宗教的方式）

sentences.en: from the way ordinary believers practice their faith.
sentences.zh: 与普通信徒实践信仰的方式之间的对比。

sentences.en: Theological doctrines can be quite complex
sentences.zh: 神学教义可能相当复杂，

sentences.en: and in some ways counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面甚至有些反直觉。

sentences.en: But sometimes we find this disconnect
sentences.zh: 但有时我们会发现这种脱节：

sentences.en: between the way that people think about their religious beliefs
sentences.zh: 人们思考其宗教信仰的方式，

sentences.en: and the way that their theological doctrines
sentences.zh: 与神学教义

sentences.en: say that they should think about their religious beliefs.
sentences.zh: 告诉他们应该如何思考宗教信仰的方式并不一致。

sentences.en: It's not always a one-on-one correspondence.
sentences.zh: 它并不总是完全一一对应的。

sentences.en: Sometimes this is half-jokingly called theological incorrectness, right?
sentences.zh: 有时这半开玩笑地被称为神学不正确，对吧？

sentences.en: So, for example, in the Abrahamic traditions,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，在亚伯拉罕诸教中，

sentences.en: particularly in Islam and some parts of Christianity,
sentences.zh: 特别是在伊斯兰教和基督教的一些流派中，

sentences.en: God should not be thought of as a person.
sentences.zh: 不应该把上帝看作是一个人。

sentences.en: God is an abstract force.
sentences.zh: 上帝是一种抽象的力量。

sentences.en: But many believers can't help but think about God
sentences.zh: 但许多信徒还是忍不住把上帝

sentences.en: as a person-like being that they can interact with,
sentences.zh: 想象成一个可以与之互动、

sentences.en: they can pray to, they can ask for forgiveness or advice, etc.
sentences.zh: 可以向其祈祷、可以寻求宽恕或建议等的人形存在。

sentences.en: So it's very much like a human-like being with extra powers.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常像一个拥有超能力的类人存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's also what allows us now to say,
sentences.zh: 是的，但这也就是为什么我们现在可以说：

sentences.en: I have a personal relationship with God, for example,
sentences.zh: 比如“我和上帝有着个人的关系”，

sentences.en: and that personal relationship is not with some abstract entity.
sentences.zh: 而这种个人关系并非与某种抽象实体建立的。

sentences.en: It's with an entity that really has very human-like capabilities.
sentences.zh: 它是与一个真正拥有极具人类特色能力的实体建立的。

sentences.en: Yes, that's correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，没毛病。

sentences.en: In many of the studies that we have done and others' work as well, we find that to the extent that people believe in more of a personal God,
sentences.zh: 在我们做过的许多研究以及其他人的研究中，我们发现，人们对个人神的信仰程度越高，

sentences.en: they seem to be more religiously committed.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎对宗教的投入度就越高。

sentences.en: It seems like one interpretation of that is that the more we entertain God as a person-like being, the more easier it is to then be religiously involved.
sentences.zh: 对此的一种解释似乎是，我们越是将上帝视为一个类人存在，就越容易参与到宗教活动中去。

sentences.en: And conversely, an abstract God, it's possible to think about it that way and people do think about it that way,
sentences.zh: 相反，对于一个抽象的上帝，虽然可以这样去想，人们也确实会这样想，

sentences.en: but that doesn't make it very compelling to then engage with such a God.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能让人对与这样一个上帝交往产生多大的兴趣。

sentences.en: There's this one amusing example that was happening in the 1990s, I believe, in Nashville, Tennessee, where a cinnamon bun was identified as being the likeness of Mother Teresa.
sentences.zh: 有一个有趣的例子，我相信发生在20世纪90年代的田纳西州纳什维尔，当时有一个肉桂卷被认出长得像特蕾莎修女。

sentences.en: Excited customers are making pilgrimages to the Bunga Java coffeehouse
sentences.zh: 兴奋的顾客们纷纷前往“爪哇面包”咖啡馆，

sentences.en: to see the marvel enshrined in a counter display.
sentences.zh: 去观看供奉在柜台展示柜里的这个奇迹。

sentences.en: The shop's manager said a customer was about to bite into the bun
sentences.zh: 店经理说，当时一名顾客正准备咬一口肉桂卷，

sentences.en: when he noticed its remarkable likeness to Mother Teresa's face.
sentences.zh: 却突然发现它惊人地酷似特蕾莎修女的脸。

sentences.en: When I teach about anthropomorphism, I show this to my students
sentences.zh: 当我讲授拟人化时，我会把这个展示给我的学生看，

sentences.en: because it's so fascinating that even a cinnabon bun
sentences.zh: 因为这太迷人了，甚至连一个肉桂卷

sentences.en: becomes an object of worship in a pilgrimage site.
sentences.zh: 也能变成朝圣之地的崇拜对象。

sentences.en: as long as it has some anthropomorphic qualities.
sentences.zh: 只要它具有某些拟人化的特质。

sentences.en: And that's what happened in this case.
sentences.zh: 这正是当时发生的情况。

sentences.en: It became a very popular destination.
sentences.zh: 它成了一个非常受欢迎的目的地。

sentences.en: Thousands of people started to go there to see the cinnamon bun,
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人开始涌向那里去看那个肉桂卷，

sentences.en: which was placed under a secure glass box.
sentences.zh: 它被放置在一个安全的玻璃盒子里。

sentences.en: It was a big phenomenon at the time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时是个轰动的现象。

sentences.en: Where do you think our capacity or our drive to anthropomorphize the world comes from?
sentences.zh: 你认为我们对世界进行拟人化的能力或驱动力是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Why would we have such a feature in the mind?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们的脑海中会有这样一种特征？

sentences.en: There are interesting theories about that in psychology.
sentences.zh: 心理学中对此有一些有趣的理论。

sentences.en: the sense of control is an important element of anthropomorphism
sentences.zh: 控制感是拟人化的一个重要元素，

sentences.en: in the sense that when we think of something as having agentic qualities,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当我们认为某事具有能动性时，

sentences.en: we feel like we can control it, we can understand it better.
sentences.zh: 我们会觉得我们可以控制它，我们可以更好地理解它。

sentences.en: If an earthquake is just a random earthquake and there's no sense to it,
sentences.zh: 如果一场地震只是一场随机的地震，没有任何意义，

sentences.en: it's very hard to understand.
sentences.zh: 那就很难理解。

sentences.en: It's also very hard to then figure out what to do.
sentences.zh: 也很难弄清楚该做什么。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if an earthquake is caused by an evil spirit or by God,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果地震是由邪灵或上帝引起的，

sentences.en: then it's understandable for our minds and also it tells us what to do maybe appease the gods
sentences.zh: 那么对我们的头脑来说它就是可理解的，这也告诉我们该做些什么，也许是安抚神灵，

sentences.en: maybe negotiate with the spirits yeah so in other words you have an angry god but maybe i will make
sentences.zh: 也许是与精灵谈判，是的，换句话说，你有一个愤怒的神，但也许我会做

sentences.en: a sacrifice that basically appeases the angry god and i suppose you could argue that it's safer
sentences.zh: 一个基本上能平息愤怒神明的祭品，我想你可以辩称，

sentences.en: almost to assume that things have agency than to assume that things don't have agency it's it's a
sentences.zh: 假设事物具有能动性，几乎比假设事物没有能动性更安全，这在某些方面是一个问题，

sentences.en: problem in some ways if you don't realize that someone, in fact, has an agenda that could hurt
sentences.zh: 如果你没有意识到某人实际上有一个可能会伤害你的议程，

sentences.en: you.
sentences.zh: 那就会出问题。

sentences.en: And in some ways, there's less of a downside in seeing agency where none exists.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，把原本不存在的东西看作有能动性，其负面影响要小得多。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Our threats and how we detect threats in the world, there's a profound asymmetry in the
sentences.zh: 关于我们的威胁以及我们如何在世界上探测威胁，存在着一种深刻的不对称性，

sentences.en: sense that it's better to err on the side of seeing something that's not there than not seeing
sentences.zh: 即宁可错杀一千，把不存在的东西看作存在，也好过

sentences.en: a threat that actually exists.
sentences.zh: 漏掉一个真实存在的威胁。

sentences.en: So if you mistake a rope for a snake, the worst thing is that
sentences.zh: 所以如果你把一根绳子错看成一条蛇，最糟糕的结果也就是

sentences.en: you're scared for a second and then you just move on with your life.
sentences.zh: 你害怕了一秒钟，然后继续过你的生活。

sentences.en: But if there is an actual snake
sentences.zh: 但如果真有一条蛇

sentences.en: and you mistake it for a rope, you might be dead.
sentences.zh: 而你把它错看成了绳子，你可能就没命了。

sentences.en: So our ancestors, according to this argument,
sentences.zh: 因此，根据这种论点，我们的祖先

sentences.en: developed an asymmetric threat detection system where it's better to be trigger happy.
sentences.zh: 进化出了一种不对称的威胁探测系统，宁可反应过度。

sentences.en: It's better
sentences.zh: 宁可

sentences.en: to, as they say, shoot and ask questions later
sentences.zh: 像他们说的那样，先开枪，以后再问问题，

sentences.en: rather than the other way around.
sentences.zh: 总比反过来要好。

sentences.en: Another facet of the mind that you and others have explored
sentences.zh: 你和他人探讨过的大脑的另一个方面

sentences.en: has to do with a concept called dualism.
sentences.zh: 与一个叫做二元论的概念有关。

sentences.en: Explain what this idea is, Ara,
sentences.zh: 请解释一下这个观点是什么，阿拉，

sentences.en: and how it affects our capacity for religious belief.
sentences.zh: 以及它如何影响我们的宗教信仰能力。

sentences.en: Dualism is the capacity that we have in our minds
sentences.zh: 二元论是我们大脑中具备的一种能力，

sentences.en: that allow us to entertain that mind stuff
sentences.zh: 它让我们能够想象精神层面的东西

sentences.en: can be distinct and separate from physical stuff.
sentences.zh: 可以独立并脱离于物质层面的东西。

sentences.en: And once our brains can do that, we can have spirits without bodies,
sentences.zh: 一旦我们的大脑能做到这一点，我们就能拥有没有肉体的灵魂，

sentences.en: we can have gods who are everywhere and are not tied to a particular physical property.

sentences.en: A variety of studies, he says, show that religious faith can help our well-being.
sentences.zh: 他说，各种研究表明，宗教信仰可以帮助提升我们的幸福感。

sentences.en: There is a link between religion and happiness and well-being.
sentences.zh: 宗教与幸福感之间存在着某种联系。

sentences.en: There are earthly benefits to religion on this planet Earth,
sentences.zh: 在这个地球上，宗教有着世俗的好处，

sentences.en: and that's why religion has survived as an important feature of human societies for as long as we know.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么宗教能够作为人类社会的一个重要特征延续至今的原因。

sentences.en: There's also been research, Ara, that looks at income levels around the world
sentences.zh: 阿拉，也有研究着眼于全球的收入水平

sentences.en: and happiness levels around the world.
sentences.zh: 以及全球的幸福水平。

sentences.en: And with some nuances, I think it's fair to say that richer countries in general
sentences.zh: 在有一些细微差别的情况下，我认为这样说算得上公正：总的来说，较为富裕的国家

sentences.en: tend to be happier than poorer countries.
sentences.zh: 往往比贫穷的国家更幸福。

sentences.en: And there are some ceiling effects and floor effects.
sentences.zh: 这其中存在一些天花板效应和地板效应。

sentences.en: But in general, it's better off to be rich than it is to be poor.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，富裕总比贫穷要好。

sentences.en: And perhaps that's not a surprising finding.
sentences.zh: 或许这并不是一个令人惊奇的发现。

sentences.en: But it's also the case that richer countries tend to be less religious than poorer countries.
sentences.zh: 但同样的情况是，较富裕的国家往往比较贫穷的国家宗教色彩更淡。

sentences.en: And that seems to now elicit a paradox here.
sentences.zh: 现在这似乎引发了一个悖论。

sentences.en: It is a paradox.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个悖论。

sentences.en: So the paradox is that if we look at countries and their happiness levels, the happiest countries are the least religious countries.
sentences.zh: 所以这个悖论就是，如果我们观察各个国家及其幸福水平，最幸福的国家往往是宗教信仰最少的国家。

sentences.en: However, individuals, at least in religious societies, they tend to be happier.
sentences.zh: 然而，个人，至少在宗教社会里，往往更幸福。

sentences.en: So how is this possible?
sentences.zh: 那么这怎么可能呢？

sentences.en: The explanation that I think is the most compelling is that as societies become wealthier, they become existentially more secure.
sentences.zh: 我认为最具说服力的解释是，随着社会变得越来越富裕，它们的生存安全感也随之增强。

sentences.en: and as a result, people have more predictable and safer lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们的生活变得更加可预测、更加安全。

sentences.en: As a result, people become less religious.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，人们变得不再那么笃信宗教。

sentences.en: Religion declines in wealthy countries.
sentences.zh: 在富裕国家中，宗教在衰落。

sentences.en: We know this.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点。

sentences.en: We've known this for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来我们一直都知道这一点。

sentences.en: There's a very powerful effect of country-level income on religious levels.
sentences.zh: 国家层面的收入对宗教水平有着非常强大的影响。

sentences.en: Religious declines as income goes up.
sentences.zh: 随着收入的增加，宗教信仰随之减少。

sentences.en: So that's one thing to keep in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以这是需要记住的一点。

sentences.en: The other thing that makes sense is that in places that don't have these features, life is not existentially secure, where there are high levels of poverty, infant mortality,
sentences.zh: 另一件合乎逻辑的事是，在那些不具备这些特征、生存缺乏安全感的地方，那里贫困率和婴儿死亡率很高，

sentences.en: income inequality levels, social safety nets are virtually absent.
sentences.zh: 收入不平等水平高，社会安全网几乎形同虚设。

sentences.en: These are the conditions where religious beliefs and practices seem to give people the most benefit.
sentences.zh: 在这些条件下，宗教信仰和实践似乎给人们带来了最大的益处。

sentences.en: So this is when and where people turn to religion to deal with these difficulties and the suffering that these conditions elicit.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就是人们在何时何地转向宗教，以应对这些困难以及这些条件所引发的痛苦。

sentences.en: So in other words, if you're a poor person and a religious person, you might be better off in a poor country rather than in a rich country?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你是一个贫穷且有宗教信仰的人，你在贫穷国家可能会比在富裕国家过得更好？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That is the case.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: This is evidence from a large-scale study by Jana Bergesel and Johan Gebauer and their colleagues, where they looked at precisely this paradox.
sentences.zh: 这是雅娜·贝尔格塞尔、约翰·格鲍尔及其同事开展的一项大规模研究提供的证据，他们正是研究了这个悖论。

sentences.en: The paradox that they were trying to explain was that you find that in wealthy countries,
sentences.zh: 他们试图解释的悖论是，你发现在富裕国家中，

sentences.en: people who are struggling economically are less happy and have less well-being than people who are struggling economically in poor countries.
sentences.zh: 那些在经济上苦苦挣扎的人，其幸福感和福祉要低于贫穷国家中同样在经济上苦苦挣扎的人。

sentences.en: You would expect intuitively that in wealthier countries, people who are struggling should be better off because they're in a wealthier country overall.
sentences.zh: 人们凭直觉会期望，在更富裕的国家里，那些苦苦挣扎的人应该过得更好，因为他们总体上处于一个更富裕的国家。

sentences.en: But that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And the explanation that they explored, of course, was that in wealthier countries, religiosity declines.
sentences.zh: 他们探讨的解释当然是，在更富裕的国家里，宗教信仰在衰退。

sentences.en: So religion is not as available as a way of coping and responding to life's adversities.
sentences.zh: 因此，宗教作为一种应对和回应生活逆境的方式，不再那么容易获得了。

sentences.en: But in poorer countries, income levels are lower, and people remain religious, and people turn to religion when they're struggling,
sentences.zh: 但在贫穷国家，收入水平较低，人们依然保持着宗教信仰，当他们苦苦挣扎时会求助于宗教，

sentences.en: and they get these benefits from their religious involvement.
sentences.zh: 并且他们从参与宗教活动中获得了这些好处。

sentences.en: There's been a fair amount of work that's been done on the subject of meaning,
sentences.zh: 关于意义这个主题已经进行了相当多的研究，

sentences.zh: 那么，我觉得我的人生对我和对他人重要吗？

sentences.zh: 我觉得自己是在带着某种热情或目标过日子吗？

sentences.en: It could be a career choice.
sentences.zh: 它可以是职业的选择。

sentences.en: It could be friends.
sentences.zh: 它可以是朋友。

sentences.en: It could be a hobby.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一个爱好。

sentences.en: So coherence, significance, and purpose together comprise the sense of meaning we have in our lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，一致性、意义重大性和目标共同构成了我们生命中的意义感。

sentences.en: And we can see how in all cases religion can provide people meaning.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到在所有情况下宗教是如何为人们提供意义的。

sentences.en: So in the case of coherence, people's religious worldviews give them a coherent understanding of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以在一致性的情况下，人们的宗教世界观赋予了他们对世界的连贯理解。

sentences.en: And also religious traditions tell people you matter.

sentences.zh: 上帝爱你，你很重要

sentences.en: or that this is all happening for a reason
sentences.zh: 或者这一切发生都是有原因的

sentences.en: Things are not chaotic.

sentences.en: So all of these are important elements

sentences.zh: 奇怪的现象。

sentences.en: world, also have high levels of mental distress and suicide.
